Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.4

What is the vertex of y=(x-5)²-7?

feedback.text: Vertex form y=(x-h)²+k gives vertex (h,k).
The sign inside the parentheses is interpreted oppositely.
The value outside the square is -7, not 7.
Both signs are interpreted incorrectly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.4

What is the axis of symmetry for y=(x+4)²+1?

feedback.text: The axis of symmetry is vertical, so it is written as x= a number.
The sign inside the parentheses is interpreted oppositely.
x+4=x-(-4), so the axis of symmetry is x=-4.
The axis is not horizontal and does not use the opposite of the inside value as a y-value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.5

What are the zeros of y=(x-6)(x+2)?

feedback.text: These reverse the signs from the factors.
Set x-6=0 and x+2=0.
The factor x+2 gives -2, not 2.
The factor x-6 gives 6, not -6.

Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.5

What is the y-intercept of y=x²+3x-10?

feedback.text: This uses the constant as an x-coordinate and reverses its sign.
The coefficient of x is not the y-intercept.
This does not come from setting x=0.
When x=0, y=-10.

answer.text: It opens downward and has a maximum at (1,6).

Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.5

The zeros of a quadratic are -3 and 5. What is the axis of symmetry?

feedback.text: One zero alone is not the midpoint.
The midpoint of -3 and 5 is (-3+5)/2=1.
This uses the difference in the wrong direction.
One zero alone is not the axis of symmetry.

Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.4

Which point is symmetric to (1,8) across the axis x=4?

feedback.text: This point lies on the axis, not the mirror image of (1,8).
Reflection across a vertical line changes the x-coordinate, not the y-coordinate.
The x-coordinate is mirrored, but the y-coordinate should remain 8.

Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q10

For y=(x+1)(x-7), what are the x-intercepts?

feedback.text: These reverse the signs from the factors.
These are written as y-intercepts, not x-intercepts.
The y-coordinate must be 0 at x-intercepts.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.4

Which feature tells where a parabola changes from decreasing to increasing when it opens upward?

feedback.text: The y-intercept is where the graph crosses the y-axis, not necessarily where direction changes.
The vertex is the turning point of the parabola.
An x-intercept is where the output is 0, not necessarily the turning point.
The leading coefficient affects opening direction and width, but the vertex locates the turn.

What is the y-intercept of y=-3x²+2x+8?

feedback.text: This places the constant on the x-axis instead of the y-axis.
The coefficient of x is not the y-intercept.
Setting x=0 gives y=8.
The leading coefficient is not the y-intercept.

Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.5

A parabola has vertex (4,-2). What is its axis of symmetry?

feedback.text: The axis of symmetry for a vertical parabola is vertical, not horizontal.
This uses the y-coordinate as the x-value.
The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex.
This uses the x-coordinate as a horizontal line.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U05_L04_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.QE.4

Which statement is true for y=4x²+1?

feedback.text: The leading coefficient is positive, so it opens upward.
In this form, the vertex is (0,1).
Every function value at x=0 gives a y-intercept.
A positive leading coefficient makes the parabola open upward.
